message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Official EPA air‑quality index (AQI) for all U.S. cities, plus pollutant breakdowns (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO). | Enter “Los Angeles” in the search box or use the map. |
| **AQICN** (aqicn.org) | Global air‑quality map with real‑time data from local monitoring stations. | Search “Los Angeles” or look at the city’s page. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily AQI updates and health advisories. | Check their “Weather” or “Health” sections. |
| **Mobile apps** (AirVisual, Plume Labs, BreezoMeter) | Push notifications for AQI changes and health recommendations. | Download the app, enable location services, and view the LA dashboard. |

**Quick tip:**  
- **AQI 0–50** – Good  
- **51–100** – Moderate  
- **101–150** – Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  
- **151–200** – Unhealthy  
- **201–300** – Very Unhealthy  
- **301+** – Hazardous  

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the AQI a few hours before you go, as it can change rapidly with traffic, weather, and wildfires.
